title: Your GitHub is your interview magnet
oneliner: More interview calls come from a GitHub that shows architecture views, demos, governance/security/observability thinking, and end-to-end system design.
says: To get more AI architect interviews, fix your GitHub: the README should contain architecture views, demos, and architecture details; the repository should show governance, security, and observability; and it should showcase your end-to-end thinking. All three are mandatory if you want more interview calls.
explained: Recruiters and hiring managers do read repos - it is the only portfolio an architect can show publicly. His checklist is really a hierarchy of proof. Architecture views prove you can design. Governance/security/observability sections prove you think like an enterprise, not a hobbyist - the exact premium from the governance reel. End-to-end thinking - problem to deployment, not a notebook fragment - proves you can ship.

Notice the consistency with his other advice: 'build your own agent' (#26) is what fills this repo; 'share your understanding' (#14) is the same instinct applied to writing. The through-line: public, inspectable evidence of real work is the engine of his whole career strategy. A thin README with clone-of-a-tutorial code fails this test on arrival.
takeaway: Audit your best repo today: README with architecture diagrams and a demo, plus explicit governance, security, and observability sections.
